complete_source.work: Vitruvius De architectura IX.8.8, entire owned Gwilt English paragraph
complete_source.text: 8. Other kinds of winter-dials are made, which are called Anaporica . They are constructed as follows. With the aid of the analemma the hours are marked by brazen rods on their face, beginning from the centre, whereon circles are drawn, shewing the limits of the months. Behind these rods a wheel is placed, on which are measured and painted the heavens and the zodiac with the figures of the twelve celestial signs, by drawing lines from the centre, which mark the greater and smaller spaces of each sign. On the back part of the middle of the wheel is fixed a revolving axis, round which a pliable brass chain is coiled, at one of whose ends a phellos or tympanum hangs, which is raised by the water, and at the other end a counterpoise of sand equal to the weight of the phellos .
complete_source.boundary: 8. Other kinds of winter-dials... through ...equal to the weight of the phellos .; no clause trimmed.

source_only_future_options.complete_text: 10. Wherefore, as the sun passing through the signs, lengthens and shortens the days and hours, so the index of the dial, entering by the points opposite the centre round which the wheel turns, by its daily motions, sometimes in greater, at other times in less periods, will pass through the limits of the months and days. The management of the water, and its equable flow, is thus regulated.

The same dial index enters through points opposite the wheel centre and moves daily, with differing periods.
The whole closing sentence introduces management of water and equable flow; it may not be omitted as mere transition.

source_only_future_options.complete_text: 11. Inside, behind the face of the dial, a cistern is placed, into which the water is conveyed by a pipe. In its bottom is a hole, at whose side is fixed a brazen tympanum , with a hole in it, through which the water in the cistern may pass into it. Within this is inclosed a lesser tympanum attached to the greater, with male and female joints rounded, so that the lesser tympanum turning within the greater, similar to a stopple, fits closely, though it moves easily. Moreover, on the lip of the greater tympanum are three hundred and sixty-five points, at equal distances. On the circumference of the smaller tympanum a tongue is fixed, whose tip points to the marks. In this smaller tympanum a proportionable hole is made, through which the water passes into the tympanum , and serves the work.
whole_obligations: Behind the dial face stands a cistern fed by a pipe.
A bottom hole and attached brazen larger tympanum admit water through its own hole.
An enclosed smaller tympanum with rounded male/female joints fits closely yet turns easily like a stopple.
The larger lip has365 equally spaced points.
